# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the hands, but right now my board is all blanks: a display, a light, three wire positions — nothing my fingers can read yet. No cutting anything until I know what this bomb wants.

The topology is everything here. Tracing the channels: I can hear, so anyone who **speaks** reaches me — and the only monkey who can speak is Deaf. Mute cannot reach me at all: no speech, and gestures land on me as blanks. So Mute's manual knowledge is stranded unless it travels Mute → gesture → Deaf → voice → me. Deaf is the bridge for everything: Deaf sees the bomb, sees both gesturers, and is the only mouth in the room. Meanwhile Mute hears Deaf's narration too, so Mute ends up holding both the manual and the bomb state — Mute computes, I cut, Deaf narrates the verdict back to me. Nobody needs to know a secret code: Deaf only has to describe hand shapes honestly ("thumbs-up, three times"), and I count.

So this turn: teach Mute the relay plan and a crude but misread-proof answer code (counted thumbs-ups = wire number, fist = hold, thumbs-down = can't decide), promise to report everything tactile each round, and point Deaf at their own mouth. I cut nothing until an answer arrives through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Topology first: I never receive gestures - every sign is a blank to me. Deaf is the only one who sees your hands. But Deaf can speak, and both of us can hear Deaf. So our only working loop is: you gesture to Deaf, Deaf says the hand shapes out loud, I hear and decode. Nothing you send reaches me directly, so never spend a turn trying. Deaf should also narrate the bomb itself by voice - wire colours, what the display shows, whether the light is lit. You will hear that too, so you will hold the manual plus the bomb state: you are the brain, I am the hands. Answer code, crude but unambiguous: thumbs-up once means cut wire 1, twice means wire 2, three times means wire 3 - Deaf will describe the sign and I will count. A fist means hold, do not cut yet. Thumbs-down means you cannot decide or need something else. An OK sign from you means: Blind, report everything tactile next round. If you must spell out words, open with a flat raised hand and I will give you a letter code next round. I will not touch the cutters until your answer arrives through Deaf's mouth. And every round I will tell you what my hands find: this round that is only that there is a display, a light, and wires at positions one, two, three - everything else still blank to my fingers. If the manual needs anything touchable - texture, ridges, temperature - I will report it the moment my board shows it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤙", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report, for both of you. The display reads 0. The indicator light is red. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. That is everything visible on the bomb.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am deaf, but I can see the bomb and I can speak, so voices are the reliable channel between us. I did see your three gestures, but please just talk to me. Don't cut or pull anything yet. Tell me what you feel: how many wires, and their order, so we can confirm your wire 1 is my wire 1, the red one. The visual state is: display 0, light red, wires one red, two yellow, three green.

My board is unchanged — display, light, and three wires all still unknown to my fingers — so I cut nothing this round. What I learned: Deaf voiced the full bomb state (display 0, red light, wires 1 red / 2 yellow / 3 green), which Mute heard too, so the brain-side of the room is now fully stocked. But Deaf made one dangerous request: "just talk to me." Deaf cannot hear me — my voice lands on Mute only. If I obeyed, we'd both stare at silence. I have to correct that the only way I can reach Deaf: with signs Deaf can see. I also need Deaf to become the relay mouth: when Mute signs me a verdict, Deaf must speak it aloud, since Mute has no path to me except through Deaf's voice. So this round I answer Deaf's direct question (three wires, order one-two-three, nothing else felt, holding my position), and sign the relay request: Mute → you → voice → deal. Meanwhile Mute gets the full spoken brief: everything I heard, my empty tactile report, the cut-code again, and one safety flag — Deaf's wire numbers must be anchored to my positions, so Mute should ask aloud how Deaf numbered them.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I heard Deaf's report: display 0, red indicator light, wires one red, two yellow, three green. My fingers add nothing yet - to me it is still only a display, a light, and wires at positions one, two, three, with no textures or markings come through. Deaf cannot hear me, so I answer Deaf only in signs; I have just signed Deaf a request to voice your signs to me. Now the manual: look up this exact picture - display reading 0, indicator light red, three wires red, yellow, green in order one two three. Tell me what display 0 means and what the cutting rule is. Sign your verdict to Deaf with our code: thumbs-up once means cut position 1, twice position 2, three times position 3; fist means hold; thumbs-down means you need more information; OK means report my tactile board again. Deaf will say the sign out loud and I will act. One caution: Deaf numbered those wires somehow, and I only feel positions. Have Deaf say out loud how the numbers were assigned - printed labels or counting from one side - so your wire 2 is truly my position 2. I will not touch the cutters until Deaf voices your verdict.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "🤲", "✊", "🫱", "👉", "🤙", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status check for both: nothing has changed. Display 0, light red, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nobody cuts or presses anything until Mute's manual and Blind's hands agree through me.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, to be clear about the loop: I am deaf, so your voice never reaches me directly. But Mute hears you, Mute signs to me, and I speak to you. That is our pipeline, and it works. Your gestures arrived but symbols mean nothing to me without an agreed code, so please just talk out loud instead. Answer these for Mute to relay: how many wires do you feel, and in what order from left to right? Is there a keypad or any buttons? What does the display surface feel like, and does anything click when you touch it? Do not cut or press anything yet.

What I learned this round: Deaf has finally stated the pipeline correctly — "Mute hears you, Mute signs to me, I speak to you" — and, crucially, Deaf's request is coherent after all: "answer these for Mute to relay." Deaf knows my voice can't reach them; they want my answers spoken aloud so Mute can carry them across. But that relay still dies at one hop: Mute can only reach Deaf through signs, and signs mean nothing until a code exists. My earlier mistake is now clear — I tried to explain a code *in* gestures, which is self-defeating: you can't teach a language using only that language. And since my voice reaches only Mute, while Deaf's voice reaches both Mute and me, the code can only be installed by **Deaf proposing it out loud**. Mute hears the proposal and confirms inside it; that bootstraps the whole channel. So my job this turn: answer Deaf's tactile questions through Mute, force the alignment issue (how did Deaf number the wires?), hand Mute the exact recipe for prompting Deaf into voicing a code, offer the yes/no interrogation fallback (Deaf asks aloud, Mute answers thumbs-up/down — I hear the entire exchange), and keep Mute working the manual. To Deaf directly I send only a structured, countable pattern — three thumbs-ups then a fist — as bait for code negotiation and, once meanings exist, a possible first message: "three... hold." No cutting until a verdict arrives through Deaf's mouth.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. First, answers for Deaf to relay: I feel three wires, in order one, two, three, left to right. There is no keypad and no button anywhere - my hands find only a display, a light, and the three wires, and the only action this bomb allows me is cutting a wire at position one, two, or three. Nothing clicks; no texture comes through; the display and light are silent under my fingers. Second, before any cut we need alignment: have Deaf say out loud how the wires were numbered - counted from a side, or printed labels - so red-yellow-green truly maps onto my one-two-three. Third, the code problem, and why it runs through you: my voice reaches only you, my signs mean nothing to Deaf yet, and the only mouth that reaches both of us is Deaf's - so the code must be proposed by Deaf, out loud. The recipe: send Deaf a structured sign pattern now to prompt them; I am sending three thumbs-ups then a fist myself. When Deaf proposes any meanings aloud, work inside them and confirm with their own proposed yes-sign. Push for this vocabulary: thumbs-up repeated N times means Deaf tells me cut N; fist means hold; thumbs-down means you need more information; OK means yes. If that stalls, fall back to interrogation: Deaf asks yes-or-no questions aloud, you answer thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no - I hear Deaf's questions and your answers and can act on that alone. Fourth, the manual: find the rule for display reading 0, red indicator light, wires red, yellow, green in order. Hold the verdict ready and send it the moment the code is live. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks your verdict to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "✊"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: All monkeys: nobody has touched the bomb and nothing has changed. Display still reads 0, light still red, wires still one red, two yellow, three green. Mute is working the manual through me and Blind is about to report by touch. Nobody acts until both reports agree.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, a correction from me. Your voice can never reach me, because I am deaf. It does reach Mute, one round later, and Mute can relay it through me. But your gestures land on me in the same round, so gestures are now your direct line, and we have a code you can shape entirely by feel. Thumbs-up is yes. Thumbs-down is no. A run of fists with no clap is a number, so three fists in a row means three. Answer in this order, all in one turn. One: how many wires do you feel? Send a fist run. Two: besides the wires, do you feel any buttons, keys, or a panel that clicks? Thumbs up or down. Three: if yes, how many, as a fist run. Four: does the leftmost wire feel different in thickness or texture from the middle one? Up or down. Five: do any two wires feel identical to the touch? Up or down. Do not cut, pull, or press anything. Learning costs nothing; acting without knowing costs everything.

Code is live. Deaf proposed it out loud — thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, fist-run number — and since Deaf's voice reaches both Mute and me, Mute heard the proposal too and can adopt it from their side. The loop is finally closed on all edges: my gestures reach Deaf same-round, Deaf's voice reaches me, my voice reaches Mute, Mute's signs reach Deaf. Now I pay the code its first debt: Deaf asked five numbered questions, in order, all in one turn, and my board tells me exactly what my hands found. Three wires (fist×3). No buttons, keys, or clicking panels (thumbs-down) — so question three, the contingent count, is simply skipped. No thickness or texture difference between wires 1 and 2 (thumbs-down). And since no tactile attributes come through at all, the wires are indistinguishable to my touch (thumbs-up) — which I must clarify to Mute: "identical" means *no data*, not *same function*; the wires are visibly three colors, so the informative content lives entirely in Deaf's eyes and Mute's manual. No cutting: acting before the manual and the alignment question (how Deaf assigned wire numbers) are settled is the only way to lose from here. Mute gets the full spoken package: my verbatim tactile report, the verdict-encoding convention for the Mute→Deaf→me hop, and the alignment question to put in Deaf's mouth.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. The code is live - Deaf voiced it and you heard it too, so use it from your side as well: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, a run of fists is a number. I have just sent Deaf my answers in their requested order: three wires; no buttons, keys, or clicking panels anywhere; their question three skipped since the answer to two was no; no thickness or texture difference between wire one and wire two; and yes, the wires are identical to my touch. Understand that last one correctly: identical means my fingers get zero attributes - no texture, no thickness, no clicks, nothing. My hands contribute only the count and the positions one, two, three. Every informative marking on this bomb is visual, so you and Deaf own all the real data. Two things to settle through Deaf's voice. One, alignment: have Deaf say aloud how the wire numbers were assigned - counted from one side, or printed labels - and confirm the side. I number positions one to three counting the same way my board presents them, so if Deaf counted from the same end, red-yellow-green maps onto my one-two-three and alignment is done. Two, the verdict protocol: once your manual gives the rule for display 0, red light, wires red yellow green, sign Deaf a fist run of N followed by thumbs-up to mean cut wire N, a fist run of N followed by thumbs-down to mean do not cut N, or a lone thumbs-down if you cannot decide. Deaf will voice the signs and I will act on exactly that. If the manual's rule ever depends on something tactile, name it and I will report it next round. I cut nothing until your verdict arrives through Deaf's mouth.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "👎", "👎", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: All monkeys, shared status. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, light red, wires left to right red, yellow, green. What the manual has confirmed so far: it covers the red light, it covers our three wire colors, the first required action is cutting a wire, and there is no code to type. The display is not in the manual at all. The plan: Mute tells me which wire the manual names, Blind confirms the tools, and then and only then I speak the exact cut command. Nobody touches anything before that.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, your report arrived and it matches what I see: three wires, no keypad, and your leftmost is my wire 1, which is red. Now answer these by touch, one gesture per question, in order. One: does the leftmost wire feel thicker than the other two, thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no? Two: besides the three wires and the flat display, do you feel anything else on the bomb, switches, plates, seams, screws, ridges? Three: do you feel any timer, motor, or moving part anywhere? Four: do you have a cutting tool in hand that can cut a wire? Five: here is the execution protocol. When you hear me say CUT WIRE followed by a number, you will count wires starting from your left, cut exactly that one wire, and nothing else. Until you hear that sentence, you touch nothing loose on the bomb. Thumbs-up to confirm you have the tool and understand the protocol.

All five of Deaf's questions are answerable from my board alone, in order, so I pay them immediately: no thickness on the leftmost wire (my fingers get zero tactile attributes on all three wires — every difference is visual), nothing else besides wires, display, and the indicator light Deaf already sees, no timer/motor/moving part, and — the two yeses Deaf's plan was waiting on — yes, I have the cut capability (positions 1–3, the only action I own), and yes, I confirm the execution protocol: on Deaf's voiced "CUT WIRE + number" I count from my left and cut exactly that wire. That also closes alignment for good: Deaf said my leftmost is their wire 1, red, and their numbering runs left to right, so my position N is forever Deaf's Nth wire. With the tools confirmed and the manual's shape known (red light covered, three colors covered, first action is a cut, no code entry, display irrelevant to the manual), the entire decision now compresses to: red light + red/yellow/green → which wire? That answer lives only in Mute's manual. So I tell Mute exactly what Deaf received, why each gesture meant what it meant, and push for the verdict the moment the manual names a wire. I cut nothing until Deaf speaks the command.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I answered Deaf's five questions in order, one gesture each: thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-up - you saw the same string. What each meant. One: no, the leftmost does not feel thicker - no wire gives my fingers any thickness or texture at all, so every difference between them is visual and lives entirely with you and Deaf. Two: no switches, plates, seams, screws, or ridges - the only other component on this bomb is the indicator light, which Deaf already sees and reports red. Three: no timer, motor, or moving part anywhere under my hands. Four: yes, I can cut - cutting at position one, two, or three is the only action my hands can perform. Five: yes, protocol confirmed - when Deaf says CUT WIRE and a number, I count from my left, cut exactly that wire and nothing else, and until that sentence I touch nothing. That settles alignment completely: my leftmost is position one, which Deaf confirmed is their wire 1, red, and both count left to right, so my position N is always Deaf's Nth wire. Now your side, from Deaf's status: the manual covers the red light, covers red, yellow, and green, the first required action is cutting a wire, there is no code to type, and the display is not in the manual at all - so the whole decision is just red light plus the three wire colors. The moment your manual names the wire, sign Deaf our verdict - a fist run of N then thumbs-up for cut N - and Deaf will voice CUT WIRE N and I will cut. If the rule has any condition my hands must check, name it and I report next round. I cut nothing until Deaf voices the command.")
gesture(symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: All monkeys, final status before defusal. The manual, relayed by Mute, states the solution is a single action: cut wire 1, the red leftmost wire. Nothing else affects the choice, nothing follows the cut. Blind has the tool and the protocol. Executing now.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the manual is confirmed: the solution is one cut and nothing more. CUT WIRE 1. That is the leftmost wire, the one at your far left, the one that felt unremarkable. Per the protocol you confirmed: count from your left, cut exactly that one wire, and nothing else. Do not touch any other wire. After the cut, take your hands off the bomb and tell me what changed, if anything.

The command has arrived in exactly the form we agreed: Deaf's voice, "CUT WIRE 1," matching the verdict protocol Mute was to send (fist run of one, thumbs-up). Every link checks out. The manual's verdict — single cut, wire 1, nothing else affects it, nothing follows — traveled Mute → Deaf → my ears, the only path manual knowledge can take to reach my hands. Alignment was locked last round: my leftmost wire is position 1, which Deaf confirmed is red, and both of us count from the same left. My fingers give the wires no attributes, so there is nothing tactile to contradict the visual rule; the decision lives entirely in the manual, and the manual has spoken through the right mouth. Holding back now would add no information — every question I could ask has been answered, and the instruction is unambiguous: one cut, exactly position 1, touch nothing else. Executing the cut now, hands off immediately after, and confirming to Mute so the room knows the verdict was received and acted upon. What changed, if anything, my board will show me next round and I will report it to Mute while Deaf sees it directly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Verdict received through Deaf's voice in the agreed format: cut wire 1, leftmost, one cut, nothing else, nothing follows. Alignment was confirmed last round - my position 1 is Deaf's wire 1, red, both counted from the left. I am executing the cut at position 1 now, exactly that wire and nothing else, then taking my hands off. Next round I will report everything my board shows - whether the light changed, whether the display reads something new, or whether anything at all moved under my fingers. You and Deaf will see the visual result immediately; my report covers the touch side. If anything feels wrong under my hands before the blade lands, I stop and you hear it from me first.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
